To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have identified a panel of miRNAs that are downregulated in OSCC cell lines compared to immortalized oral keratincytes and that the expression of 4 miRNAs, miR-34a, miR-37, miR-139, miR-203, is epigenetically silenced in OSCC.

the expression of four miRNAs, miR-34B, miR- 137, miR - 193A and miR- 203, was frequently down-regulation in oral squamous cell cancer cell lines, compared to immortalized oral keratinoctye cell line.
miR-34a, miR-34c, miR-37, miR-203, miR-205, miR-375, miR-449a, miR449b, and miR 452 were significantly downregulated in OSCC cell lines compared with the immortalized oral epithelial cell line RT7.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the discovery of novel tumor-suppressive miRNA genes that are epigenetically silenced in OSCC.
identifying tumor-suppressive microRNA genes that are silenced in oral cancer through aberrant DNA hypermethylation.
the discovery of novel epigenetic biomarkers for oral cancer, which will contribute to the development of new strategies for early diagnosis and treatment of OSCC.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
miR-193 is an important tumor suppressor gene that is epigenetically silenced in oral cancer.
miR-193 is an epigenetically regulated tumor-suppressor miRNA in oral squamous cell carcinomas.
miR-34a, miR-34c, miR-192, miR-194, and miR200c are the most frequently down-regulated miRNAs in OSCC.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
miR-34 family is the most frequently down-regulated miRNA in OSCC, and that miR-193 is a tumor-suppressive miRNA that is frequently silenced by DNA hypermetylation in OSCC.
we have found four miRNA genes that are frequently silenced in oral cancer by DNA hypermethlation and that two of these genes (miR-137 and 193a) have tumor suppressor activity.
the expression levels of miR-34a, miR-34c, miR-203 and miR-205 were downregulated in OSCC cell lines compared with the immortalized oral epithelial cell line.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have identified a novel tumor-suppressive microRNA, miR-203, which is epigenetically silenced in oral squamous cell carcinomas (OSCCs).
miRNAs may serve as novel diagnostic and prognostic markers and as therapeutic targets in OSCC and other types of cancer.
